request.description:
AllowAnonymous. Code can't be produced by Postman - it comes from redirecting a real browser through Microsoft's sign-in with PKCE first. Send the frontend to:

https://login.microsoftonline.com/{TenantId}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize  
?client_id={ClientId}  
&response_type=code  
&redirect_uri=[http://localhost/auth](http://localhost/auth)  
&response_mode=query  
&scope=openid profile email offline_access  
&code_challenge=d8u9K3bpfN5jJTaQxkiQ33ippLXy-OONYvhVMFumhNY  
&code_challenge_method=S256  
&state=12345

{ClientId}/{TenantId} are this app's real Microsoft app registration values - real secrets, not something to hardcode here; read them from this app's own .docker/.env (Development) or Kubernetes secret (Staging/Production). state, redirect_uri and code_challenge are fixed test values (nothing server-side checks state; redirect_uri must be registered in this app's Microsoft app registration's redirect URI allowlist for the exchange to actually succeed; code_challenge is the SHA-256/base64url hash of the fixed Auth.Microsoft.CodeVerifier collection variable's default value) - all three are baked in so this URL works as-is once redirect_uri is registered; only replace them (redirect_uri on its own, or code_verifier/code_challenge together as a matching pair) if you want a real per-attempt exchange instead. Microsoft then redirects back to redirect_uri with ?code=... - set Auth.Microsoft.Code from that before running this (RedirectUri/CodeVerifier are already preset to match). Sets User.Id, Auth.AdminToken and Auth.AdminRefreshToken from the response.
